claim: Hanbok rental in Seoul costs roughly 15,000-20,000 won and grants free entry to all five royal palaces plus hair styling and accessories.
quote: For 15,000-20,000 won — less than the price of a nice lunch — you get a complete hanbok outfit, Korean hair styling, accessories, and free entry to all five royal palaces.
note: Free palace entry requires wearing both top (jeogori) and bottom; regular palace ticket is only ~3,000 won.

claim: The 2026 Changdeokgung Moonlight Tour runs April 16-May 31, costs KRW 30,000, lasts ~100 minutes, and is sold exclusively on Creatrip starting April 2, 2026; foreigner sessions are limited and sell out fast.
quote: Changdeokgung Moonlight Tours will take place from April 16th – May 31st... The admission price to the Changdeokgung tour is KRW 30,000, with a limit of two tickets per buyer.
note: Reservation-only; bring foreign ID plus screenshot of voucher; check-in 20 min before.

claim: Jogyesa Temple in Insadong offers overnight templestay (1 night/2 days, ~50,000-100,000 KRW) and shorter day programs; popular slots fill up, so booking ~1 month ahead via eng.templestay.com is advised.
quote: Popular spots like Jogyesa fill up fast, so booking at least 1 month in advance is recommended through the Official Templestay Booking Website (eng.templestay.com). Prices are approximately 50,000 to 100,000 KRW per adult for a 2-day, 1-night stay.
note: Overnight program includes lotus lantern craft, monastic meals, optional 108 prostrations and 4:25am ceremony; foreigner 'One-day Zen Discovery' also available.

claim: Dragon Hill Spa in Yongsan is a 24-hour jjimjilbang charging roughly 15,000 won on weekends and 12,000 won on weekdays, with admission including spa access, sleeping rooms, clothes and towels.
quote: The entrance fee is 15,000 won per person on weekends and 12,000 won on weekdays... includes access to all spa locations and sleeping rooms, clothes and towels, as well as hairdryer and pillows.
note: Open 24/7; extra 1,000 won per hour after default duration.

claim: The National Museum of Korea in Yongsan has free admission to permanent exhibitions, open 10am-6pm most days and until 9pm on Wed and Sat.
quote: Admission is completely free to the permanent exhibitions. Only special exhibitions require entry fee... 10 a.m. – 6 p.m. (Sun.–Tue. & Thu.–Fri.) / 10 a.m. – 9 p.m. (Wed. & Sat.).
note: Located 137 Seobinggo-ro, Yongsan-gu; Ichon Station Exit 2.

claim: Leeum Museum of Art offers free permanent (traditional) collection by reservation, while special and contemporary exhibitions cost 18,000 KRW general admission (9,000 KRW discounted).
quote: The permanent traditional art collection is free, though reservations are required... general admission to the Leeum Samsung Museum of Art is priced at 18,000 KRW. There are discounted rates available for youth, teenagers, and seniors at 9,000 KRW.
note: Reservation required even for free collection; digital guides free in English.

claim: The War Memorial of Korea in Yongsan has free admission, open 9:30am-6:00pm and closed Mondays, near Itaewon.
quote: The War Memorial of Korea is open 9:30 AM - 6:00 PM, closed Mondays... Admission is free!
note: Last admission 5pm; plan 2-3 hours; located 29 Itaewon-ro, Yongsan-gu.

claim: The non-verbal Nanta cooking-themed percussion show in Myeongdong starts from ~37,500 won and plays at the UNESCO Building on Myeongdong-gil.
quote: Nanta show tickets in Seoul's Myeongdong start from ₩37,500... located at 3F, UNESCO Building, 26, Myeongdong-gil, Jung-gu, Seoul, Korea.
note: Blends traditional Korean rhythms with acrobatics; note Myeongdong Nanta Theater is distinct from Myeongdong Art Theater.

claim: Bukchon Hanok Village hosts traditional craft workshops (hanji paper, Korean knotwork, mother-of-pearl) running roughly 1-2 hours for 10,000-40,000 won, with materials and master instruction included.
quote: Expect ₩10,000-40,000 for 1-2 hour sessions, ₩60,000-150,000 for intensive programs, with prices including materials and master instruction.
note: Donglim Knot Workshop knotting passed down 4 generations; studios set in genuine hanok.

claim: Seoul K-pop dance experiences at HiKR Ground are ~2-hour beginner classes near Jonggak Station that teach hit choreography and produce an edited video shot in themed rooms.
quote: This 2-hour experience is perfect for anyone, even if you've never danced before, where you'll learn the highlight choreography of the latest K-pop hit in a private studio near Jonggak Station.
note: Small groups up to 6; HiKR Ground itself is a free tourism-center K-pop attraction with music-video-set photo zones.
